history.period: 11th-12th century (approx. 900 years old; some sources suggest 12th century)
history.summary: A 900-year-old Shaivite temple in the Unkal locality of Hubballi, built in the Chalukya era on the lines of the Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal temples. The shrine is unusual for its four entrances (one in each direction) and for housing two large Shivalingas - the presiding Chandramouleshwar facing east and the four-faced Chaturmukha Linga - with two Nandi statues at the entrance. Its walls and black-granite pillars carry fine sculptures, including dancing Ganesha. Local legend says the temple was built overnight by anonymous artisans (some versions credit the sculptor Jaknacharya and his son) and therefore stands incomplete, with no traditional gopura. It is a Monument of National Importance and a Protected Monument under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites Act (1958), maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India. NOTE: the CSV's 'Hubli' is approximate - the temple stands in the Unkal area of Hubballi, ~3 km north of the city centre, near Unkal Lake.

name: Chandramouleshwara Temple
town_description: Hubballi (Hubli), twin city of Dharwad, is the commercial and transport hub of North Karnataka and its largest city by population. Once a 12th-century trading post under the Chalukyas, it is today a major railway and industrial centre. The Unkal area, on the old Pune-Bangalore highway, is known for Unkal Lake and the ancient Chandramouleshwara Temple.

travel.railway: Hubli Junction (UBL) ~5 km; Unkal station is the nearest halt (verify)
travel.road: Near Unkal circle on the old NH4 (Pune-Bangalore road), ~3 km north of Hubli city centre, beside Unkal Lake
